name: the Ethiopian eunuch
overview: The Ethiopian eunuch is a male official serving under Queen Candace, as noted in Acts 8:27. His role as an official highlights his position of authority and trust within the Ethiopian court. No further tribal or familial details are provided in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: He is referred to by the title 'the eunuch,' which means a court official or eunuch, indicating his role and status rather than a personal name. This title is given in Acts 8:27 and is not a name given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for the Ethiopian eunuch beyond his service to Queen Candace as an official. There are no additional relationships noted.
scriptureSignificance: The Ethiopian eunuch holds significance in the biblical narrative as a high-ranking official who encounters the gospel message, representing the reach of Christ's salvation beyond Israel. His role as an official of Queen Candace connects him to a wider, Gentile context, emphasizing the inclusive nature of the gospel. His story illustrates God's guidance in bringing the gospel to diverse peoples.
